LESSON: LISTENING 14.1.1 CONSONANT SOUNDS AND INTONATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.1: Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can one learn to correctly pronounce words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ from a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. pronounce words with the sounds /v/, /f/, /n/ and /ŋ/ in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use correct intonation for yes/no and wh- questions in varied contexts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in a conversation.  Search from print and non-print sources for tongue twisters with some of the target sounds and say them for enjoyment. Learners who may not turn pages to use page-turners or be supported by peers. They could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to record findings.  Watch a video or listen to a recording or conversation on outdoor games and group the words in a table according to the following target sounds: v/ as in very; /f/ as in ferry /n/ as in been an /ŋ/ as in being. Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing/listening. How can one learn to correctly pronounce words? 135  Listen to, and model native speaker clips with the target sounds in words. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they model and allow them more time.  Work with peers to practise the pronunciation of words with the target sounds and record themselves,  Share the clips for peer review,  Listen to an audio or a dramatised conversation on outdoor games in which yes/no and wh- questions are used and point out whether a rising or falling intonation is used,  Practise articulation of Yes/No and WH- questions with the appropriate intonation in dialogues,  Write, dramatise and record a dialogue using words with the target sounds as well as Yes/ No and WH- questions and 136 share with peers for review. Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they dramatise. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use an alternative functional part of the body to perform the task.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening 14.1.1 Consonant Sounds and Intonation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Digital literacy is enhanced as the learner uses digital tools to record themselves and shares dramatised dialogues.

 Self-efficacy is developed as the learner documents their successes when writing and dramatising the conversations.

Values:
Respect is achieved as the learner works with peers to practise the pronunciation of words and record themselves.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Health Education is developed as the learner listens to dramatised conversations on outdoor games leading to body fitness.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of pronunciation and intonation to learning pronunciation of sounds in Kiswahili.
